rounds.text: Insilco Ltd presents a severe disconnect between its market valuation and its fundamental ability to generate returns, as evidenced by a deeply negative Return on Capital Employed (ROCE) of -39.8% [E4]. This lack of profitability is further highlighted by a Return on Equity (ROE) of -41.1% [E5]. Despite these negative returns, the stock trades at an aggressive Price-to-book ratio of 9.84x, which is based on a book value of only ₹ 0.85 [E1]. Investors receive no income for holding this risk, as the dividend yield remains at 0.00% [E3]. Conceded: [E6], [E7], and [E8] show compounded profit growth of 14% over five years, 19% over three years, and 16% over the trailing twelve months respectively. Nevertheless, this growth has not yet resulted in positive returns, leaving the ₹ 52.4 Cr market capitalization [E2] unsupported by the current performance of the business.
